subject: bug in m*ply with global variables

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: bug in m*ply with global variables
parts:
Dear list,

Consider the following code,

x = 5
y = 2

foo <- function(a="x"){
switch(a, "x" = x,
"y" = y)
}

params <- expand.grid(a=c("y","x"))

mdply(params, foo)

a V1
1 y 5
2 x 2

As far as I can see it's a bug (which I noticed, very puzzled, when
two facets of my ggplot had their labels swapped...)

The reason I'm doing this switch() construct is that I need to pass
data.frames to the function through mdply, so I just pass their name.

Thanks,

baptiste

Hi:

This, OTOH, appears to 'work':

foo <- function(a) switch(a, 'x' = x, 'y' = y)
a <- c('y', 'x')

> mdply(as.data.frame(a), foo)

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: bug in m*ply with global variables
parts:
OK, it's probably got nothing to do with plyr, sorry.

Consider this,

foo(factor('x', levels=c('y', 'x')))

# 2

so, basically switch, when given a factor, considers the integer codes
rather than the string levels :(

Sorry for the noise. I'll post something to R-help just to make sure.

baptiste
